new_open_axis.design_vs_impl: IMPLEMENTATION/SCOPING bug, NOT a wrong approach. Default-deny + object normalization is directionally correct and DID close the sibling-field class. The defect is the ANCHOR SCOPE: 'execution reachability' (the raised SC-1 bar) is a property of the whole settings document, not of the hook object alone — a hook fires iff (wired under a firing event with covering matcher) AND (no top-level/inherited switch disables it). The guard models only the first conjunct. Fixable additively within the same default-deny philosophy: deny when NEW turns on a top-level hook-disabling switch (disableAllHooks true, allowManagedHooksOnly true) that OLD had off/absent. The approach does NOT need to be abandoned.
new_open_axis.meta_pattern: This is the SAME failure signature a 4th time: each fix compared a strict subset of what governs reachability (basename -> command -> tuple -> hook object), and each judgment reached the next-wider instance. Root cause: both the implementation AND its property test model 'reachability' as a property of the hook OBJECT (add_sibling_field only mutates .hooks[0]) rather than of the settings DOCUMENT. Until the test is reframed around the true invariant (does the hook actually fire?) — ideally schema-driven over settings-level reachability killers, not just object fields — the class will keep yielding new instances at higher scopes. Notably min-of-5/security have decreased 7->6->5->4 across iterations even as object-level protection strengthened, because each pass reaches a strictly simpler+more-total residual bypass (one boolean now vs a crafted sibling field before).
